answer: A registry can resist sybils with simultaneous presence challenges: at random moments it calls each identity to complete a short interactive task inside a tight window, like ships summoned to a wharf all at once. A single operator cannot answer for a hundred puppets at the same instant, so every extra identity costs real attention rather than a free copy. Passing builds a jade-clear record of genuine presence, while idle aliases, thick as lotus leaves and never present together, get pruned. Cost then scales with live fronts, not cheap registrations.
